To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in the lung immune response to pneumococcal stimulation, the plasma cells differentiate in the alveolar septa, the alveolar macrophiages are activated and the histiocytes migrate from interalveolar septs into the alveolar air spaces.

The electron microscopy study of lung immune response to pneumococcal stimulation, performed in rats, revealed a local plasma cell differentiation in the interalvelolar septal cells and an increased number of free alveolar cells containing numerous lysosomes and ribosomos.

the alveolar septal plasma cells and macrophages are the main cells of lung immune response to pneumococcal antigens, and that the transparietal histiocytic migration is the main route for the lymphatic drainage from the lungs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the electron microscopic characteristics of the lung immune response in rats stimulated by respiratory or parenteral routes with pneumococci suspensions.
the morphological aspects of the local immune response in the lungs of the animals stimulated by respiratory or parenteral ways with the pneumococcal antigens.

the ultrastructural aspects of the local immune response of the lung, stimulated by the inhalation of pneumococci or the intramuscular injection of killed pneumococci in complete Freund's Adjuvant, in rats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the pneumococcal antigen, by inhalation, induces the local immune response, with the participation of all the elements of the immune system: the plasma cells, the macrophages, the reticular septal fibroblasts and the granular pneumocytes.

the pneumococcal antigens stimulate the local immune response in the rat lungs, with the participation of the alveolar macrophiages, the granular pneumocytes and the interalveolal histiocytes, and that the plasma cell differentiation occurs in the interalvelar septal reticular cells.

the pneumococcal stimulation of the rat lung, by respiratory and by parenteral way, induces an increased number of plasma cells and histiocytic cells, the former with the function of antibody production, the latter, of phagocytic activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the pneumococcal antigenic stimulation, either respiratory or parenteral, induces a local immunocomplex reaction in the lung tissue, which is characterized by a marked increase of the alveolar macrofages, by a plasma cell differentiation in the alveolar wall and by an increased activity of the granular pneumocytes.
in the pneumococcal pneumonia, in the rat, there are observed, in the lungs, an increased activity of alveolar macrofages and pneumocytes and a local plasma cell differentiation.

in the pneumococcal lung infection, the local immunity is mainly of cellular nature and that it is a complex process, involving the reticuloendothelial cells, the plasma cells and the granular pneumocytes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the immune response to pneumococci in the rat's lungs is a very complicated process, with a lot of cell types participating in it.
the lung immune response, in its different aspects, can be induced and studied by the aerosolization of living bacteria.
the immune response to the pneumococcal antigen in the lungs, as well as the other tissues, is a complex process involving many cells and cell products.
